content: Acyclovir is an antiviral medication used to treat infections caused by specific viruses, including outbreaks of genital herpes. While it is not a cure for these infections, it helps reduce the severity and duration of outbreaks. Acyclovir promotes faster healing of sores, prevents the formation of new sores, and alleviates pain and itching. It may also shorten the duration of pain after the sores heal. This medication is typically taken orally, with or without food, as directed by a healthcare provider, usually 2 to 5 times daily. Acyclovir works best when started at the first sign of an outbreak. The dosage depends on the patient’s medical condition and response to treatment. To maintain its effectiveness, it is important to take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course. Common side effects of acyclovir include nausea, diarrhea, headache, and vomiting. Serious allergic reactions are rare. Patients should inform their healthcare provider if they have any allergies, particularly to acyclovir or valacyclovir, or if they have other medical conditions. Acyclovir does not prevent the spread of genital herpes. To reduce the risk of transmission, patients should avoid sexual contact during outbreaks or when symptoms are present and consistently use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activity. During pregnancy, acyclovir should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Patients should discuss the risks and benefits of using this medication with their healthcare provider. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of acyclovir or increase the risk of side effects. Patients should provide their healthcare provider with a complete list of all medications and supplements they are taking. Acyclovir is similar to valacyclovir, and care should be taken to avoid duplication of therapy. In case of an overdose, immediate medical attention is required. In the U.S., patients can contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, they can call 1-844-764-7669. Acyclovir should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and not in the bathroom. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into drains unless instructed to do so. Proper disposal of expired or unused medication is recommended. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about acyclovir. Patients should consult their healthcare provider for complete information tailored to their specific health needs.
